note: Last-author surname -> training/co-authorship lineage id, for leave-one-lineage-out holdouts and for lineage-clustered bootstrap. Bibliographic knowledge only: who trained with whom and who publishes together. It encodes no anatomical outcome and no claim about any result. Pooling rule applied: a lineage is the senior author's own doctoral or postdoctoral parent within this field, EXCEPT that a lab independent long enough to have trained its own cohort gets its own id (so Reddien, Newmark, Rink, Petersen, Pearson, Salo, Bartscherer and Aboobaker are their own lineages rather than being folded into Sanchez Alvarado). Levin trainees and Marchant trainees are pooled as instructed. Surnames whose lineage is uncertain, and ambiguous or very common surnames, get their own id rather than a guess. Keys are lower case; accented spellings are listed beside their ASCII forms because the harness strips non-ASCII characters when canonicalising. A surname absent from this map is its own lineage by default in harness/derive_features.py, and the count of unmapped labs is printed as lab_not_in_lineage_map. Two deliberate choices a reviewer should know about: (1) pooling trainees with their parent lab reduces the number of independent clusters, which makes UNTESTABLE verdicts more likely but prevents one lineage from counting as several confirmations; (2) Cebria trained in both Barcelona and Kyoto and is assigned to the Barcelona lineage.
